questions.question:
What will come in place of question mark (?) in the given equation?

39 ? 11 ? 33 ? 117
If 4 @ 9 # 3 = – 2 and 11 # 2 @ 6 = 7, then 14 @ 3 # 7 = ?
questions.solution:
The explanation is as follows,

Here @ and # is used as a code for – and + respectively. i.e.

4 @ 9 # 3 = – 2 → 4 – 9 + 3 = – 5 + 3 = – 2.

11 # 2 @ 6 = 7 → 11 + 2 – 6 = 13 – 6 = 7.

Similarly,

14 @ 3 # 7 = ? → 14 – 3 + 7 = 11 + 7 = 18.

Hence, 18 is the correct alternative.

questions.question:
In the following question, select the missing number from the given alternatives.

120, 119, 115, 106, 90, ?
questions.solution:
The relation between the numbers is as follows,

120 – 1² = 120 – 1 = 119.

119 – 2² = 119 – 4 = 115.

115 – 3² = 115 – 9 = 106.

106 – 4² = 106 – 16 = 90.

90 – 5² = 90 – 25 = 65.

Hence, the next number is 65.

questions.question:
In the following question, select the word which cannot be formed using the letters of the given word.

TECHNOLOGICAL
questions.solution:
Let’s check each option,

1) LOGIC → can be formed as TECHNO**LOGIC**AL.

2) LOAN → can be formed as TECH**N**O**LO**GIC**A**L.

3) HATER → cannot be formed as there is no ‘R’ in TECHNOLOGICAL.

4) COLOGNE → can be formed as T**EC**H**NOLOG**ICAL.

Hence, HATER can’t be formed from the word TECHNOLOGICAL.

questions.question: The ratio of present ages of A and B is 5 : 7. If the age of B after 10 years will be 31 years, then what is the present age (in years) of A?
questions.solution:
Given data,

Ratio of present ages of A and B is 5 : 7.

Let the present age of A be 5x and that of B be 7x.

The age of B after 10 years will be (7x + 10) which is equal to 31 years.

Thus,

7x + 10 = 31 → 7x = 21 → x = 3

x = 3

Present age of A is 5x → 5 x 3 = 15 years.

Thus, 15 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts, read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:** I. All blue are black. II. Some blue are yellow.

**Conclusions:** I. All blue are yellow. II. Some black are yellow.
questions.solution:
Consider the following least possible Venn diagram,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d0cfd31c6ab752dbab02c939990419187f830cc2b738f014f91e5e1e38460fdd.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. All blue are yellow → False (It is possible but not definite).

II. Some black are yellow → True (It is definitely true as the part of blue which are yellow is also black as all blue are black).

Hence, __**only conclusion II **__follows.

questions.question: In a certain code language, "ADD" is written as "8" and "SUB" is written as "41". How is "MUL" written in that code language?
questions.solution:
Here, if A is 1, B is 2, C is 3 and so on Z will be 26.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e1c94b7f893e02635eaafb26dfd964e61e9615da89eadbea45cfaace47d5fbec.png] 

 

The code used here is one less than the total sum of the numbers which comes in place of each letter i.e.

ADD → A = 1, D = 4, D = 4 → (1 + 4 + 4) – 1 = 9 – 1 = 8

SUB → S = 19, U = 21, B = 2 → (19 + 21 + 2) – 1 = 42 – 1 = 41

Similarly,

MUL → M = 13, U = 21, L = 12 → (13 + 21 + 12) – 1 = 46 – 1 = 45

Thus, **45** is the correct alternative.
